provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: My values ladder
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state values.
The pupils should be able to list good values.
Introduction:
We learn about good values.
Values help us to be good children.
Content:
Values are good things we do.
Examples of values are honesty kindness and hard work.
We make a ladder of values.
The top value is the most important value for you.
Class activity:
Each pupil draws a ladder.
Pupils write their top value on the top step.
Evaluation questions:
What is a value?
Name one good value.
What is your top value?
Summary:
Values help us to be good children.

topics.title: Leadership is service
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain service.
The pupils should be able to act as serving leaders.
Introduction:
We learn about leaders.
Good leaders serve others.
Content:
Leaders are people who guide us.
Great leaders help others.
Leadership is not about bossing people around.
It is about serving others.
We can all be serving leaders in our class.
Class activity:
Pupils take turns to be class leader for five minutes.
The leader helps others with their work.
Evaluation questions:
What makes a good leader?
Give an example of serving others.
How can you be a serving leader?
Summary:
Good leaders serve others.

topics.title: Integrity
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to define integrity.
The pupils should be able to identify acts of integrity.
Introduction:
We learn about doing right.
Doing right when nobody watches is important.
Content:
Integrity means being good inside and outside.
It is doing right even when no one is watching.
We show integrity by being honest always.
Example: returning lost money to the teacher.
Class activity:
Pupils act out scenes showing integrity.
Example: finding a toy and giving it back.
Evaluation questions:
What is integrity?
Give an example of integrity.
Why is integrity important?
Summary:
Integrity means doing right always.

topics.title: Respect for all work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify different types of work.
The pupils should be able to show respect to workers.
Introduction:
We see workers every day.
All work is important.
Content:
Every work has dignity.
Examples: market seller farmer driver teacher.
We respect all workers by greeting them.
We say thank you when they help us.
Class activity:
Pupils practice greeting different workers.
Example: Good morning market woman. Thank you for the food.
Evaluation questions:
Name a worker you see.
Why should we respect all workers?
How do you show respect to workers?
Summary:
We respect all workers.

topics.title: Patriotism
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state ways to show love for Nigeria.
The pupils should be able to recite the national pledge.
Introduction:
We live in Nigeria.
We must love our country.
Content:
Patriotism means loving Nigeria.
We show love by keeping Nigeria clean.
We throw rubbish in the bin.
We say the pledge with meaning.
The pledge promises to be good citizens.
Class activity:
Pupils recite the national pledge together.
Pupils draw pictures of keeping Nigeria clean.
Evaluation questions:
What is patriotism?
How do you show love for Nigeria?
What do we promise in the pledge?
Summary:
We love Nigeria by keeping it clean.

topics.title: Stewardship
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain stewardship.
The pupils should be able to care for school property.
Introduction:
We have things to care for.
We must take care of them.
Content:
Stewardship means caring for things.
We care for school property.
Example: do not break chairs.
We care for the earth.
Example: do not litter.
Class activity:
Pupils clean the classroom together.
Pupils arrange books properly on shelves.
Evaluation questions:
What is stewardship?
How do we care for school property?
How do we care for the earth?
Summary:
We care for things around us.

topics.title: Peer pressure basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify peer pressure.
The pupils should be able to say no respectfully.
Introduction:
Friends sometimes ask us to do things.
We must make good choices.
Content:
Peer pressure is when friends ask us to do something.
My choice is my responsibility.
If something is wrong we say no.
We say no with respect.
Example: No thank you I will not join you.
Class activity:
Pupils practice saying no in role-play.
One pupil asks another to do something wrong.
The other pupil says no politely.
Evaluation questions:
What is peer pressure?
Why is my choice my responsibility?
How do you say no respectfully?
Summary:
We say no to wrong things.

topics.title: Media choices
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify good media programmes.
The pupils should be able to tell adults about troubling content.
Introduction:
We watch TV and play games.
We must choose good things.
Content:
Media means things we watch and hear.
We choose good programmes.
Good programmes teach us good things.
If we see something troubling we tell adults.
Example: tell mummy about scary things.
Class activity:
Pupils look at pictures of TV programmes.
Pupils say which ones are good and why.
Evaluation questions:
What is media?
How do we choose good programmes?
What do we do if we see something troubling?
Summary:
We choose good media.

topics.title: Graduation gratitude
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to express gratitude to teachers and parents.
The pupils should be able to make a thank you card.
Introduction:
We are graduating soon.
We must thank people who helped us.
Content:
We say thank you to our teachers.
Teachers teach us many things.
We say thank you to our parents.
Parents take care of us.
We can write thank you cards.
Class activity:
Pupils make thank you cards for teachers and parents.
They draw pictures and write thank you.
Evaluation questions:
Who do we thank at graduation?
Why do we thank them?
How do we show gratitude?
Summary:
We thank our teachers and parents.

topics.title: Revision and values day
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to present their values ladder.
The pupils should be able to identify good character traits.
Introduction:
We revise what we learned.
Today we celebrate good values.
Content:
We present our values ladder.
We show our top value.
We have graduation character awards.
We give awards for good behavior.
Example: honesty award kindness award.
Class activity:
Pupils come forward to present their values ladder.
The class gives a clap for each pupil.
Evaluation questions:
What is your top value?
Name one good character trait.
Who gets a character award?
Summary:
We celebrate good values and character.
